Observed Notebook 4 pattern: Occupation groups show different ANC pathway profiles rather than a simple socioeconomic gradient. Professional/clerical women had particularly high ANC entry and early initiation, while differences among other groups varied across later stages.
How to use in programme review: Use occupation to ask whether work schedules, livelihood demands, seasonality, clinic hours or opportunity costs help explain an identified access or continuity problem.
Evidence needed before interpretation: Clinic opening hours, waiting time, livelihood patterns, work flexibility and qualitative evidence from women.
Boundary: Occupation categories are not an ordered socioeconomic scale and should not be interpreted as causal effects.

Observed Notebook 4 pattern: Differences are visible across ANC entry, early initiation and later attainment. Protestant women had approximately national-level entry but lower early initiation and lower ANC8+ after ANC4+, whereas the pattern among Muslim women also included weaker entry.
How to use in programme review: Use the signal to investigate whether geography, community context, communication, service organization or other correlated conditions help explain an observed pathway difference.
Evidence needed before interpretation: Regional and residence distribution, service context, community engagement information and locally appropriate qualitative evidence.
Boundary: Religion is treated as a contextual marker, not as an intrinsic barrier, mechanism or programme target.

Observed Notebook 4 pattern: ANC entry was lower among women reporting that the pregnancy was wanted no more. Progression to ANC4+ was also lower among women reporting 'wanted later' or 'wanted no more' than among those reporting 'wanted then'.
How to use in programme review: Use reproductive context as a secondary lens when examining early engagement and continued ANC participation.
Evidence needed before interpretation: Family-planning context, counselling pathways, social support, pregnancy acceptance and qualitative evidence.
Boundary: This was a deliberately limited deep dive. Pregnancy intention is retrospectively reported and should be interpreted cautiously.
